Which of the following best describes the fallacy of amphiboly?
Option A: Using emotionally charged languages to create an impression about the subject of a claim, without making an argument that the language fits the subject.
Option B: Referring to an act committed by an opponent in negative terms while referring to the same act committed by the arguer or supporters in favorable terms.
Option C: Using grammar and punctuation in a way that a statement may have multiple interpretations, so it's not really clear what is meant.
Option D: Changing the meaning of a word or phrase from one part of the argument to another.
